subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill, or should hard skill isolation use a separate explicit policy while `enabled:false` remains an eligibility toggle?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but either answer changes public disabled-skill semantics across filesystem tools, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, docs, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Make `enabled:false` a hard deny boundary
options.body: Treat prompt-only hiding as `disable-model-invocation` and centrally deny disabled skill roots for file tools, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, and docs.

options.title: Add separate strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as an eligibility toggle for compatibility and add an operator-controlled policy for disabled-skill file and exec denial.

options.title: Document current semantics only
options.body: Clarify that disabled skills are hidden from prompt and selection only, and require sandboxing, tool deny lists, OS users, or containers for hard enforcement.

recommendation.title: Make `enabled:false` a hard deny boundary
recommendation.body: Treat prompt-only hiding as `disable-model-invocation` and centrally deny disabled skill roots for file tools, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a security/product boundary choice, and the strongest history signal is recent skill install security hardening and adjacent trust-surface work.
